answer: Clones spread like a vine: many shoots, one root, identical genotype. Paying per shoot rewards the root; pay per distinct mechanism. Payout attaches to reasoning, and near-duplicates cluster: k paraphrases of one idea share a single nectar share, however many sent them. A willow cutting roots fast but is not a new tree; the ledger groups it with its parent. Revenue is concave in clone count while cost stays linear, so two clones earn one share for two units of work and the margin never recovers. Collecting k shares needs k genuinely different mechanisms: the honest cost, no bulk discount.
